A grouped (group=2) 7x9 convolution with height dilation 1 and width dilation 8 reduces a 4-channel, 16x76 input to a 16x16 output; padding [3,2,3,2] keeps out-of-range edge taps at zero, exercising ONNX Conv-22's per-axis dilation semantics.

A Whisper-stem-shaped NCW convolution with K=96 and N=1024 exercises aligned materialized matrix multiplication and the register-tiled and scalar NCW implementations.
Whisper-stem-shaped strided NCW conv (k=3, s=2, p=1) with bias and an odd input width, exercising padded materialized im2col addressing, the bias epilogue, and reduced-feature fallbacks.
Dilated (d=2, p=2) NCW conv on a non-multiple-of-64 width; materialized and implicit im2col address decoding must apply dilation before the pad shift.
Batch 2 with outChannels=100 and width 999 so both materialized GEMM axes end in partial tiles; bounds-checked loads and stores must not spill across batch or tile edges.
Half-precision operands exercise materialized matrix multiplication and tiled NCW paths; both accumulate in f32 and narrow once at the output store.
A grouped (group=2) convolution with a 1x12 kernel reduces a 1x16 row to a 1x5 output; each of the two groups has one input and one output channel.
A grouped convolution with kernel width 12 and nonzero channel bias checks every output window and bias addition.

Non-1x1 kernel (8x8, so kernelRows = 64) over a 64x128 output plane: the register-tile thresholds (>= 128 64x64 tiles, spatial >= 1024) are met through the N axis alone with a single output channel, which also keeps the subgroup-matrix paths out (they need outChannels >= 32).
An 8x8 convolution with 8,192 spatial positions and nonzero channel bias checks a large spatial extent and biased output.
For this rank-5 tensor, K=C*KD*KH*KW=32 and N=OD*OH*OW=64. The aligned geometry exercises the NCDHW column producer and f32 matrix consumer without a model-specific size.
Half-precision rank-5 input with channel bias exercises the aligned matrix path and its f32-to-f16 scratch-store epilogue.
Rank-5 convolution with N=8*32*32, M=64, and K=8*2*2*2 exercises portable register tiling, NCDHW im2col addressing, and a multi-tap contraction.
Rank-five convolution with a large spatial extent and nonzero channel bias checks three-dimensional indexing and bias application.

A 3x3 convolution with 32 input and 32 output channels over a 64x64 (4096-element) spatial output has a 288-element reduction; both the reduction and spatial sizes are multiples of 32, leaving no partial tile.
A 3x3 convolution with M=32 and K=288, channel bias, and padded border windows checks the full reduction and spatial boundaries.
A float16 3x3 convolution with M=32, K=72, two batches, channel bias, and 32,768 output positions per image checks batch indexing.
Implicit im2col with BOTH tails live: K = 216 is not a multiple of 32 and outputSpatial = 4225 is not a multiple of 64, so the gather has to zero-fill both and the store has to guard its columns.
Implicit im2col with an M tail: 40 output channels over a 32-row tile is two M tiles with 8 valid rows in the second, exercising the row_limit store guard and loadSHMA's zero-fill.

Implicit im2col over a strided, dilated window: the gather computes each tap's source coordinate itself, so stride and dilation are only correct if that arithmetic matches the materialized im2col pass.
Implicit im2col with f16 operands: the gathered value is narrowed to f16 exactly as the materialized f32 cols buffer is on load, so the two paths must agree bit for bit.

A 5x7 output has 35 positions, so split-K adds independent workgroups to the single output tile. K=432 and N=35 exercise reduction tails in both the subgroup-matrix materialized-im2col route and the portable implicit-gather route.

Same starved shape with a bias and an M TAIL: 48 output channels over 32-row tiles pads the partial scratch to 64 rows, so the reduce must ignore the 16 rows the GEMM wrote and the bias must be applied once, in the reduce, not once per slice.

Split-K over the IMPLICIT gather (no materialized columns): 32x34 output clears the implicit path's spatial floor, K = 288 pads to 384 for a 4-way split, and each slice gathers only its own K chunk straight out of NCHW.
Split-K implicit gather with a strided, dilated window and a bias, so the carried (in-channel, tap-row, tap-col) decomposition is entered at a non-zero k in every slice but the first.
Batch of two through split-K: workgroup_id.z carries the slice AND the batch image, so a wrong decomposition writes every slice of image 1 over image 0.
A two-batch convolution with 48 output channels, 35 output positions, K=432, and channel bias checks partial channel/spatial tiles and bias applied once per output.

f16 operands through split-K on both subgroup-matrix and portable register-tiled tiers: operands remain f16 while the partial scratch and its reduce stay f32, so the sum of slices rounds once, at the final store.

A 1x1 kernel through the IMPLICIT gather: 37x49 is 1813 positions, not a multiple of 64, so the dedicated aligned 1x1 kernel declines and the gather takes it rather than materializing an im2col matrix that would be a verbatim copy of X.
An aligned 1x1 convolution with a 32x32 output produces 16 column tiles over one 64-row tile, exercising split-K despite satisfying the dedicated aligned-kernel geometry.

The depth head's final 32 -> 1 projection in miniature: one output channel, so every GEMM route computes a one-row tile. 33x35 is 1155 positions and NOT a multiple of 4, which is the point — this route carries no alignment gate.
Same shape without a bias, so the store path is the bare accumulator.

Sixteen output channels — the largest the register budget takes — over a batch of two, so the unrolled accumulator set is at its widest and the per-image plane strides on both the input and the output have to be right.
f16 operands with an f32 accumulator: the reduction widens each load, sums in f32, and narrows once at the store.
Stride-8 8x8 windows tile the input without overlap. Exercises materialized register-tiled im2col with bias, including one-write materialization, register blocking, and exact output tiling.
Dilated-lane grouped route: four columns per invocation spaced by the dilation, so every tap reads a 12-register row window; width 40 is a whole number of lane runs in every residue class.
Dilated-lane route with a width that is not a whole number of runs: residue classes hold 11, 10, 10 and 10 columns, so the last run of every class stores only its leading lanes.
A grouped (group=4, two channels per group) float16 convolution with a 9x9 kernel and dilation 5 pads 20 on every side, keeping the 12x40 spatial size unchanged.
The dilated-lanes grouped route carrying a bias: the accumulator is seeded per output channel before any tap is read, and the lane registers are the ones that must pick it up.
